7/10 MATCH under tubuild verify, with the three DIFFs all reading `objisolate: _ZTV15daObjWc_Obj03_c: unexpected reloc type=2 addend=0` on D1, D0 and classInit. That is a verify-path artifact, not a defect: running `tubuild verify ov029/daObjWc_Mizu_c` against the ALREADY-LANDED, CI-green src/game/actors/d_a_obj_wc_mizu.cpp produces the identical shape (6/9 MATCH, the same message on D1/D0/classInit) and main builds 106/106 exact with that file. tools/objisolate.py demands `addend >= VTABLE_PREAMBLE` only for a _ZTV symbol it is EXTERNALISING; in production the deadstrip-data disposition drops it instead, where addend 0 is the correct spelling. SUPERSEDES the earlier text of this note, which claimed `10/10 MATCH, all three checks clean -- D0 reproduced from a single real ~daObjWc_Obj03_c() via a fully TU-local C++ class`: that described the pre-promotion hand-assembled shadow, which carried its own `THIS TU MUST NOT BE PROMOTED` banner because ordinals [2], [3] and [4] had been degraded to func_<addr> raw-pointer-arithmetic placeholders. The TU was reconstructed from the real named-member src/ sources instead. tools/rombuild.py -j16 is the gate that matters. Note the bookkeeping asymmetry this creates: daObjWc_Mizu_c.json still records `functions_matched: 9` and `relocation_destinations_verified: PASS`, because those fields were machine-written from its PRE-promotion shadow, which still spelled the vptr as `&_ZTV14daObjWc_Mizu_c[2]`. This manifest's 7/10 and FAIL were written from the promoted file. The two TUs are equally healthy; only obj03's numbers were taken after the spelling change. No gate reads either field.

PROMOTION (this is the note to read first). Two conditions had to be settled, exactly as on the sibling ov029/daObjWc_Mizu_c. (1) EMISSION ORDER. The cartridge keeps D1 at 0x02111728, BELOW D0 at 0x02111760, while a real `daObjWc_Obj03_c::~daObjWc_Obj03_c()` member makes mwccarm emit the D2/D1/D0 triple as one group in the order D0-then-D1; objisolate refuses that with `requested functions are not emitted in ROM order`, and the group also carries an unhomed D2. Both variants are therefore written as separate `// @symbol` bodies under their mangled names in src/game/actors/d_a_obj_wc_obj03.cpp, read off the cartridge with tools/disasm.py (ov029 base 0x021111a0). That costs the CONVERTED tier's no-raw-offset and no-mangled-refs criteria for those two functions, banked in config/converted-backslide-exceptions.jsonl. (2) NO VPTR BIAS. symbols.txt records _ZTV15daObjWc_Obj03_c at 0x02113db4 and that IS the address point -- D1's literal pool word at 0x0211175c is exactly 0x02113db4 -- so every vptr store names the symbol with addend 0. The `&_ZTV15daObjWc_Obj03_c[2]` spelling is refused by production isolation with `intact multi-symbol object has undefined RTTI addend 8; text-only production isolation cannot rewrite it`.

WHY THE DESTRUCTOR IS DECLARED LAST IN include/daObjWc_Obj03_c.h, and where the 9 compiler_only_output entries come from. Nothing defines ~daObjWc_Obj03_c() as a C++ member (see the previous note), so the class's vtable and RTTI have no key function to home them. Whether mwccarm emits them here at all turns on WHERE the destructor is declared inside the class body: measured on daObjWc_Mizu_c, declared FIRST the TU emits 0 data symbols, moved after the other members it emits the full set. The first shape is not harmless -- it drops _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV15daObjWc_Obj03_c out of the set of ROM data any source verifies, and tools/validate_merge.py ratchets on that count with no escape hatch (`ROM data verified from source fell from 604 to 603 symbol(s)` on pull request #2184). The 9 licensed entries are this class's own three plus the vague-linkage RTTI passengers of the base chain dActor_c / fBase_c / dBase_c, which ride along in the same object. include/daObjWc_Mizu_c.h and include/daObjWc_Obj04_c.h have the same shape for the same reason.
